notes.meaning: God told Moses to chisel two new stone slabs and make a wooden chest to hold them. This took place after Moses pleaded for the people, showing God's mercy in renewing the covenant after the golden calf.

God promised to write the exact same words on the new tablets that were on the first ones Moses broke. This was a clear sign that God's anger had turned away and he was reconciled to his people. It showed that the Lord is willing to give failing people a second chance.
Moses obeyed God by making a chest out of durable acacia wood and shaping two stone tablets like the first ones. He then carried the stones up Mount Sinai so God could write his law upon them.

The Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on the stone tablets just as he had spoken them from the fire at Mount Sinai. God then gave the tablets back to Moses, showing that his holy standard had not changed.

Moses came down the mountain and placed the stone tablets into the wooden chest as the Lord commanded. The tablets remained safely stored there for generations as a lasting reminder of God's covenant with Israel.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: In Catholic tradition, the ark represents Christ, and the tablets inside show that Christ is the true author of the Law.

notes.meaning: Moses recalls Israel traveling to Moserah, where Aaron died and his son Eleazar succeeded him as high priest. Even after Aaron's failure with the golden calf, God showed great mercy by continuing the priesthood so the people still had a mediator to pray for them.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars view this travel note as an insertion from the Priestly source (P) rather than part of Moses' original speech.

notes.meaning: The Israelites continued their journey from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a place blessed with flowing streams of water. Even in the dry wilderness, the Lord was faithful to provide refreshment for his people.

The Lord set apart the tribe of Levi for special holy duties. They were appointed to carry the ark of the covenant, serve before the Lord as ministers, and pronounce blessings over the people in his name.

Because the Levites were dedicated to sanctuary service, they were given no territory of farmland like the other tribes. Instead, the Lord himself was their inheritance, providing for their daily needs through the tithes and offerings brought by the people.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Early church teaching applied the landless status of the Levites to Christian clergy, arguing that bishops and priests should be supported by the offerings of the faithful rather than secular work.

notes.meaning: Moses reminds the people that he stayed on the mountain forty days and nights in prayer, just like the first time. The Lord heard his earnest intercession and agreed not to destroy the nation for their rebellion.

The Lord told Moses to get up and lead the people forward to possess the Promised Land. This command proved that God had fully pardoned Israel and would keep his covenant promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Moses asks what the Lord requires in return for all his mercy and forgiveness. God asks his people to revere him, walk in his ways, love him, and serve him with their whole heart and soul.
Israel was called to obey all of the Lord's commandments for their own good. God does not give his laws to weigh people down, but to protect them and help them flourish.

The entire universe belongs to the Lord, including the highest heavens and the earth with everything in it. Because God owns all creation, he was under no obligation to pick any one nation over another.

Even though all nations belong to God, he chose to set his special love on Israel's ancestors. He selected their descendants above all other peoples, not because they earned it, but purely out of his own good pleasure.

Moses tells the people to circumcise their hearts and stop being stubborn. Outward religious ceremonies mean nothing to God unless people turn away from sin and have clean, receptive hearts toward him.

differ.view: Reformed Christians teach that this command exposes human inability to obey on our own, pointing to our need for God's sovereign grace to renew the heart.
Methodists emphasize Moses' direct call for people to actively cleanse their hearts and renounce sinful attitudes in response to God's grace.

notes.meaning: The Lord is the supreme ruler over all powers in heaven and earth, great, mighty, and awesome. He is completely fair, never shows favoritism to the powerful, and cannot be bribed.
The Lord protects the vulnerable, securing justice for orphans and widows who have no earthly defender. He also loves foreigners who live in the land, providing them with food and clothing.

God commands the Israelites to love foreigners and treat them with kindness. They were to remember their own suffering as mistreated outsiders in Egypt, which should make them quick to show compassion to others.

The people must revere the Lord alone, serve him with sincere obedience, cling tightly to him, and take oaths only in his name. Clinging to God means trusting him completely and refusing to turn to any false gods.
The Lord is Israel's true glory and the only one they should praise. He proved his power to them by performing great and awe-inspiring wonders right before their eyes.

When Israel's ancestors originally went down into Egypt, there were only seventy people in all. Now, God has multiplied them into a massive nation as numerous as the stars, fulfilling the promise he made to Abraham.
